audits.title: EP.WE.467A Snapshot Audit on the Compliance of Postoperative ERAS Protocol Following the Resumption of Elective Colorectal Surgical Operations in the COVID-19 era
audits.setting: District general hospital, Northampton General Hospital

cycle1.result: Mean compliance 4.91/7 (70%); no nasogastric tube 96%; opioid avoidance 8%; early IV fluid stop 61%; catheter removal 57%; oral intake by day 1 78%; mobilised by day 3 91%.

audits.other_findings: Higher compliance was associated with shorter length of stay (p = 0.01).
audits.citation: Roslan F, Balsom S, Rajangam A, Evans J, Ihedioha U. EP.WE.467A Snapshot Audit on the Compliance of Postoperative ERAS Protocol Following the Resumption of Elective Colorectal Surgical Operations in the COVID-19 era. Br J Surg. 2021;108(Suppl 7).

audits.title: 733 ERAS Audit: Junior Doctor Compliance with the Elective Colorectal Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) Pathway at Bristol Royal Infirmary
audits.standard: Elective colorectal ERAS pathway: early postoperative nutritional drinks and avoidance of postoperative opioids
audits.setting: Colorectal surgery department, Bristol Royal Infirmary, elective ERAS patients

cycle1.result: Early postoperative nutrition and/or solid food in 60 (68.2%); nutritional drinks prescribed for 39 (44.3%), average 3 days to prescribe; systemic opioids avoided in 7 (7.9%).

audits.intervention: Face-to-face education for new colorectal junior doctors and posters in the doctors' office.
audits.other_findings: 104 patients identified, 16 excluded for insufficient data. Second cycle planned.

audits.title: 1041 Audit of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) Protocol in Elective Colorectal Surgery (A Loop Audit)
audits.standard: ERAS guidelines for elective colorectal surgery

cycle1.result: Overall adherence 63.9% (pre-admission 59.2%, pre-operative 73.9%, intra-operative 70.1%, post-operative 52.7%); no ERAS anaesthetic component; mean LOS 9.8 days.

audits.title: 1296 A Closed Loop Audit to Evaluate the Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) Protocol in a Tertiary Oncoplastic Breast Reconstruction Unit
audits.setting: Tertiary oncoplastic breast reconstruction unit (Sheffield Teaching Hospitals / Nottingham University Hospitals); breast free flap reconstruction

cycle1.result: Proforma in notes 0%; anti-emetics 32%; anti-inflammatory plus PPI 32%; day 1 trial without catheter 0%; day 2 drain documentation 26%; mean stay 5.5 days.

audits.intervention: ERAS proforma covering pre-operation to day three

cycle2.result: Proforma in notes 92%; anti-emetics 100%; anti-inflammatory plus PPI 100%; day 1 trial without catheter 50%; day 2 drain documentation 100%; mean stay 3.75 days.

audits.other_findings: 31 patients in total across both cycles; analgesia, laxatives and enoxaparin were prescribed in 100% before and after.

audits.title: OGC SO23 - Audit on Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) in Oesophago-gastric Resections for Cancers
audits.standard: Trust ERAS protocol for oesophagectomy and gastrectomy (oral intake, drain, catheter and epidural removal, mobilisation, discharge medications)
audits.setting: Nottingham University Hospitals, high-volume oesophago-gastric resection unit

cycle1.result: Oral diet started on time 85%; epidural removal 52.6% (95% within 24 h); catheter 55% (90%); apical drain 55.6% (100%); basal drain 53.8% (85.7%); abdominal drain 81.8% (90.9%); daily mobilisation 65%; VTE prophylaxis 100%; discharge medications 86.7% to 100%.

audits.other_findings: All mobilised within four days; mean stay 9 days post-oesophagectomy; 3.2% emergency department return rate.

audits.title: 1091 An Audit to Evaluate the Effectiveness of the Implementation of an Enhanced Recovery Programme (ERP) Discharge Checklist for Elective Colorectal Cancer Resection Patients Is on Length of Stay in a District General Hospital
audits.setting: St Richard's Hospital, Chichester, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Previous audit found delayed discharge in over 50% of elective colorectal patients; 46% discharged on day checklist completed; median LOS 5 days; catheter removed day 1 in 63%.

audits.intervention: Introduction of an ERP discharge checklist.

cycle2.result: Median LOS 4 days; 61% discharged on the day the checklist was completed; 80% catheter removed on day 1.

audits.other_findings: Commonest reasons for delay were weekends (6) and comorbidities (6); weekend discharge strategy planned.
audits.citation: Sloan E, Scott B, Wright F, Greenfield D, Chase T, Limb C, et al.. 1091 An Audit to Evaluate the Effectiveness of the Implementation of an Enhanced Recovery Programme (ERP) Discharge Checklist for Elective Colorectal Cancer Resection Patients Is on Length of Stay in a District General Hospital. audits.title: 746 Optimising Delivery of Postoperative ERAS Pathways in Colorectal Surgery: A Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: Local standards based on international ERAS guidelines (medication and analgesia prescribing, nutrition, mobilisation, catheter and PCA duration)
audits.setting: Colorectal department, Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals, elective ERAS patients

cycle1.result: Of 51 on regular medications, 37% had them prescribed on the day of surgery; reason for extended catheter and PCA use missing in 45% and 74%.

audits.intervention: MDT-developed admissions protocol with flowchart at workstations, ERAS patients highlighted on handover documents, and ward-round templates.

cycle2.result: Prescribing of regular medications on day of surgery improved to 62%.

audits.other_findings: Documentation improvement noted in early results; full re-audit analysis ongoing.
audits.citation: Jones-Anderson N, McKeever M, Cullen T. 746 Optimising Delivery of Postoperative ERAS Pathways in Colorectal Surgery: A Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Project. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.242.

audits.title: TPT 1.12 Closing The ERAS Compliance Gap in Colorectal Surgery: A Completed Audit Cycle Highlighting Persistent Intra-Operative Variation
audits.standard: ERAS protocol elements (pre-, intra- and post-operative)
audits.setting: George Eliot Hospital, elective colorectal resections

cycle1.result: Counselling documentation 6.25%; pre-operative documentation 93.75%; fasting 87.5%; carbohydrate drink 75%; regional anaesthesia and normothermia 100%; NG tubes 25%; drains 14/16; opioids 100%; POD1 mobilisation 75%.

cycle2.result: All pre-operative measures 100%; mobilisation within 24 hours 85%; liquids by POD1 95%; solids by POD3 85%; median LOS 5 days; drains 85%, NG tubes 80%, opioids 100%.

audits.other_findings: Drain and NG tube use and universal opioid use remained high and are targets for the next cycle.

audits.title: EP 349 Audit of Updated ERAS Guidelines Followed in Elective Colorectal Surgery in a Teaching Hospital
audits.standard: ERAS 2025 guidelines (10 of 23 recommendations with high-grade evidence)
audits.setting: Elective colorectal surgery, teaching hospital, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: More than 90% compliance in PONV prophylaxis, NG tube removal, multimodal analgesia, post-op enteral nutrition, IV antibiotics and VTE prophylaxis; mechanical bowel prep routinely prescribed in more than 85% of resections (not recommended); more than 78% minimally invasive; 73% no drain.

audits.other_findings: All patients receiving mechanical bowel prep had oral antibiotics.
